meaning: Agree to a request or demand.
japanese: 要求や申し出を受け入れる。
cue: A union asked for a change and management agreed. Report it formally.
reply: The board acceded to the request for longer notice.
replyJapanese: 理事会は、通知期間を延ばす要望を受け入れました。
transferCue: Describe a landlord agreeing to a repair.
transferReply: He finally acceded to our request for a new boiler.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はようやく、新しいボイラーの要望を受け入れました。
nuance: Inseparable and formal, usually in writing. Agree to is the everyday version.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない改まった表現で、文書で使うことが多い。日常では agree to を使う。
contrast: Accede to is formal agreement to a demand; consent to is formal permission.
contrastJapanese: accede to は要求を受け入れること。consent to は許可を与えること。

meaning: Be relevant to a particular person or case.
japanese: 特定の人や場合に当てはまる。
cue: A colleague asks whether a rule covers part-time staff.
reply: The policy applies to everyone on a contract.
replyJapanese: その規定は、契約のある全員に当てはまります。
transferCue: Explain an exception to a discount.
transferReply: The offer doesn't apply to sale items.
transferReplyJapanese: この割引は、セール品には適用されません。
nuance: Inseparable. Apply to also means submitting an application, which the subject makes clear.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。apply to には「応募する」の意味もあり、主語で区別できる。
contrast: Apply to covers a case; apply for asks to be given something.
contrastJapanese: apply to は当てはまること。apply for は応募して求めること。

meaning: Invite someone to come into your home.
japanese: 家の中へどうぞと招き入れる。
cue: A neighbour is standing at your door in the rain.
reply: Don't stand there — let me ask you in.
replyJapanese: そんなところに立っていないで、中へどうぞ。
transferCue: Describe a visit that became longer than planned.
transferReply: She asked us in and we stayed two hours.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女が招き入れてくれて、2時間も長居しました。
nuance: Separable: ask them in. Informal and specific to your own home or room.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：ask them in。くだけた表現で、自分の家や部屋についてのみ使う。
contrast: Ask in invites someone indoors; ask over invites them to visit at all.
contrastJapanese: ask in は中へ招き入れる。ask over は家に来るよう誘うこと。

meaning: Expect something when planning.
japanese: あらかじめ見込んでおく。
cue: A job took twice as long as you expected. Describe it.
reply: We hadn't bargained for the rain.
replyJapanese: 雨のことまでは見込んでいませんでした。
transferCue: Describe an unexpectedly warm reception.
transferReply: I got more help than I bargained for.
transferReplyJapanese: 思っていた以上に、手を貸してもらえました。
nuance: Inseparable and almost always negative or with more than. On is an equally common alternative.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、否定形か more than と一緒に使うことがほとんど。on も同じくらいよく使う。
contrast: Bargain for is expecting in advance; allow for is building margin into a plan.
contrastJapanese: bargain for は事前に見込むこと。allow for は計画に余裕を持たせること。

meaning: Produce something quickly without much care.
japanese: 手早く、ざっと作り上げる。
cue: A rough draft is needed within the hour.
reply: I'll bash out a first version before lunch.
replyJapanese: 昼までに、ざっと初稿を作ります。
transferCue: Describe writing a quick note.
transferReply: She bashed out a summary in ten minutes.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は10分で、要約をざっと書き上げました。
nuance: Separable: bash it out. Informal and British, and it accepts rough quality openly.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：bash it out。くだけたイギリス英語で、粗さを前提にした言い方。
contrast: Bash out is quick and rough; work up develops something carefully.
contrastJapanese: bash out は手早く粗く作る。work up は丁寧に作り込む。

meaning: Settle somewhere to sleep, or become established.
japanese: 寝床につく。また、うまく定着する。
cue: Describe a night in a crowded house.
reply: We bedded down on the floor with spare blankets.
replyJapanese: 余った毛布を敷いて、床で眠りました。
transferCue: Describe a new process after a few weeks.
transferReply: The new rota is starting to bed down.
transferReplyJapanese: 新しい当番表が、少しずつ定着してきました。
nuance: Intransitive. Two senses: settling to sleep, and a system becoming routine. British in the second sense.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。「寝床につく」と「制度が定着する」の2つの意味があり、後者はイギリス英語。
contrast: Bed down settles for the night or becomes established; settle in adjusts to a new place.
contrastJapanese: bed down は寝床につく、または定着する。settle in は新しい場所に慣れること。

meaning: Hide something completely, or stop yourself thinking about it.
japanese: すっかり覆い隠す。記憶から締め出す。
cue: Describe fog on a mountain walk.
reply: The cloud blotted out the whole valley.
replyJapanese: 雲が谷全体を覆い隠しました。
transferCue: Describe trying not to think about something.
transferReply: I tried to blot out the memory of that interview.
transferReplyJapanese: あの面接の記憶を、頭から締め出そうとしました。
nuance: Separable: blot it out. Used for light, views and memories alike.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：blot it out。光や景色、記憶のいずれにも使う。
contrast: Blot out hides completely; block out can also mean reserving time.
contrastJapanese: blot out は完全に覆い隠す。block out には時間を確保する意味もある。

meaning: Cover a window or door with wooden boards.
japanese: 窓や戸を板でふさぐ。
cue: Describe a shop that closed last winter.
reply: They boarded up the windows in November.
replyJapanese: 11月に、窓が板でふさがれました。
transferCue: Describe preparing for a storm.
transferReply: We boarded up the shed before the wind arrived.
transferReplyJapanese: 風が来る前に、物置を板でふさぎました。
nuance: Separable: board it up. Usually about empty buildings or storm protection.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：board it up。空き家や、嵐への備えについて使うのがふつう。
contrast: Board up covers an opening with wood; brick up fills it permanently.
contrastJapanese: board up は板で塞ぐ。brick up はれんがで恒久的に埋める。

meaning: Become stuck and unable to make progress.
japanese: 行き詰まって、前に進めなくなる。
cue: A discussion is stuck on minor wording. Describe it.
reply: We got bogged down in the wording again.
replyJapanese: また言い回しの議論で行き詰まりました。
transferCue: Describe a project that lost momentum.
transferReply: The build bogged down over the planning permission.
transferReplyJapanese: 建築許可の件で、工事は行き詰まりました。
nuance: Very often passive: get bogged down in. In introduces the detail that traps you.
nuanceJapanese: get bogged down in の受け身の形で使うことが非常に多い。足を取られる対象は in で示す。
contrast: Bog down is being stuck in detail; grind to a halt is stopping altogether.
contrastJapanese: bog down は細部で身動きが取れなくなること。grind to a halt は完全に止まること。

meaning: Register your arrival, or reserve a time for something.
japanese: 到着を届け出る。予約を入れる。
cue: A colleague asks about arranging a service visit.
reply: I've booked the engineer in for Tuesday morning.
replyJapanese: 技術者を火曜の午前に予約しました。
transferCue: Describe arriving at a hotel late.
transferReply: We booked in just before midnight.
transferReplyJapanese: 深夜になる直前に、チェックインしました。
nuance: Separable: book him in. British; American English usually says check in or schedule.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：book him in。イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語ではふつう check in や schedule と言う。
contrast: Book in reserves a slot or registers arrival; book up means everything is taken.
contrastJapanese: book in は枠を予約する、到着を届け出る。book up は満席・満室になること。

meaning: Decide at the last moment not to do something because you are afraid.
japanese: 怖じ気づいて、直前でやめる。
cue: You planned to ask a question publicly but did not. Admit it.
reply: I bottled out at the last second.
replyJapanese: 最後の瞬間で、怖じ気づいてしまいました。
transferCue: Describe someone who withdrew from a challenge.
transferReply: Two people bottled out before the jump.
transferReplyJapanese: 跳ぶ直前に、2人が怖じ気づいて辞退しました。
nuance: Intransitive, informal and British. Of introduces what you avoided.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけたイギリス英語。やめた対象は of で示す。
contrast: Bottle out is losing nerve at the last moment; back out withdraws from an agreement.
contrastJapanese: bottle out は土壇場で怖じ気づくこと。back out は合意から降りること。

meaning: Face criticism confidently instead of apologising.
japanese: 悪びれずに、堂々とやり過ごす。
cue: Someone kept a firm position despite obvious embarrassment. Describe it.
reply: He brazened it out and never mentioned the error.
replyJapanese: 彼は悪びれず押し通し、誤りには触れませんでした。
transferCue: Describe a company's response to criticism.
transferReply: They brazened out the whole story rather than issuing a correction.
transferReplyJapanese: 訂正を出さず、彼らは堂々と押し通しました。
nuance: Separable and usually with it: brazen it out. Critical of the lack of apology.
nuanceJapanese: 分離でき、ふつうは it を伴って brazen it out と言う。謝らない態度への批判を含む。
contrast: Brazen out refuses to show shame; ride out simply survives a difficult period.
contrastJapanese: brazen out は悪びれず押し通す。ride out は困難な時期をやり過ごす。

meaning: Fill an opening permanently with bricks.
japanese: れんがで塞いで、恒久的に埋める。
cue: Describe an old doorway in a building.
reply: That doorway was bricked up years ago.
replyJapanese: あの戸口は、何年も前にれんがで塞がれました。
transferCue: Describe a renovation decision.
transferReply: We bricked up the side window to gain wall space.
transferReplyJapanese: 壁面を広げるため、横の窓を塞ぎました。
nuance: Separable: brick it up. Permanent, unlike boarding a window temporarily.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：brick it up。一時的な板張りと違い、恒久的な処置を指す。
contrast: Brick up is permanent; board up is a temporary covering.
contrastJapanese: brick up は恒久的。board up は一時的に覆うこと。

meaning: Move along to make room for someone.
japanese: 詰めて、場所を空ける。
cue: A friend arrives late and there is one space on the bench.
reply: Budge up a bit and she can sit here.
replyJapanese: 少し詰めてくれれば、彼女もここに座れます。
transferCue: Describe a crowded sofa.
transferReply: Everyone budged up and we all fitted.
transferReplyJapanese: みんなが詰めてくれて、全員座れました。
nuance: Intransitive, informal and British. Almost always a friendly request among people sitting.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけたイギリス英語。座っている人同士の親しいお願いとして使うのがほとんど。
contrast: Budge up makes room on a seat; move over shifts aside more generally.
contrastJapanese: budge up は席を詰める。move over はもっと広く、脇へどくこと。

meaning: Fasten a piece of clothing with buttons.
japanese: ボタンを留める。
cue: A child is heading out on a cold morning.
reply: Button up your coat before you go.
replyJapanese: 出かける前に、コートのボタンを留めなさい。
transferCue: Describe getting ready for a formal event.
transferReply: He buttoned up his shirt and straightened his tie.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はシャツのボタンを留め、ネクタイを直しました。
nuance: Separable: button it up. Informally, button up can also mean stop talking.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：button it up。くだけた言い方では「黙る」の意味にもなる。
contrast: Button up fastens buttons; do up fastens any kind of clothing.
contrastJapanese: button up はボタンを留める。do up は留め具全般に使える。

meaning: Pay someone to stop opposing you.
japanese: 金を渡して、反対をやめさせる。
cue: A story alleges payments to silence critics. Describe the claim.
reply: The article claims the objectors were bought off.
replyJapanese: その記事は、反対者が金で黙らされたと主張しています。
transferCue: Describe why you distrust a settlement.
transferReply: It looks less like agreement and more like buying people off.
transferReplyJapanese: 合意というより、金で黙らせたように見えます。
nuance: Separable: buy them off. Always disapproving, and it implies improper payment.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：buy them off。つねに否定的で、不適切な支払いを含意する。
contrast: Buy off silences opposition with money; buy out purchases a share of a business.
contrastJapanese: buy off は金で反対を抑える。buy out は事業の持ち分を買い取る。

meaning: Sleep outdoors, or wait somewhere for a long time.
japanese: 野外で寝泊まりする。長時間そこで待つ。
cue: Describe a summer with children.
reply: We camped out in the garden for three nights.
replyJapanese: 3晩、庭で寝泊まりしました。
transferCue: Describe people queuing for tickets.
transferReply: Fans camped out overnight for the box office.
transferReplyJapanese: ファンは窓口の前で、一晩中待ち続けました。
nuance: Intransitive. Beyond literal camping, it describes waiting somewhere for a long time.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。実際の野営のほか、長時間そこで粘ることも表す。
contrast: Camp out sleeps or waits outdoors; hole up shuts yourself away indoors.
contrastJapanese: camp out は屋外で寝泊まり・待機する。hole up は屋内にこもる。

meaning: Exchange something for money, or profit from a situation.
japanese: 換金する。状況を利用して利益を得る。
cue: Someone sold shares at a good moment. Describe it.
reply: She cashed in her shares before the fall.
replyJapanese: 彼女は下落の前に、株を現金化しました。
transferCue: Describe a shop benefiting from an event.
transferReply: The cafés cashed in on the festival crowds.
transferReplyJapanese: カフェは、祭りの人出をうまく利益に変えました。
frame: Cash something in / cash in on something
nuance: Separable when exchanging: cash it in. Cash in on something means profiting, sometimes critically.
nuanceJapanese: 換金の意味では分離できる：cash it in。cash in on something は利益を得る意味で、批判的にもなる。
contrast: Cash in exchanges for money; cash in on takes advantage of a situation.
contrastJapanese: cash in は換金する。cash in on は状況を利用して得をする。

meaning: Get rid of something, or untie a boat.
japanese: 捨て去る。また、もやいを解く。
cue: Someone left an old reputation behind. Describe it.
reply: The town has cast off its industrial image.
replyJapanese: あの町は、工業の町という印象を脱ぎ捨てました。
transferCue: Describe leaving a harbour.
transferReply: We cast off at six in the morning.
transferReplyJapanese: 朝6時に、もやいを解いて出発しました。
nuance: Separable when it has an object. Cast is irregular and unchanged in the past: cast.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語があるときは分離できる。cast は不規則変化で、過去形も cast のまま。
contrast: Cast off discards something deliberately; shake off escapes something following you.
contrastJapanese: cast off は意図的に捨て去る。shake off は追ってくるものを振り切る。

meaning: Formally accuse someone, or give them a duty.
japanese: 正式に告発する。また、任務を与える。
cue: A committee was given a specific responsibility. Describe it.
reply: The group was charged with reviewing the whole policy.
replyJapanese: その部会は、方針全体の見直しを任されました。
transferCue: Describe a formal report's wording.
transferReply: The report charges the department with poor record-keeping.
transferReplyJapanese: 報告書は、記録管理の不備について当該部署を指弾しています。
nuance: The person goes between charge and with. Formal, with a legal sense and a duty sense.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は charge と with のあいだに置く。改まった表現で、法的な告発と任務付与の両方の意味がある。
contrast: Charge with formally accuses or assigns; accuse of is only about wrongdoing.
contrastJapanese: charge with は告発にも任命にも使う。accuse of は非難だけに使う。

meaning: Cut something into small pieces.
japanese: 細かく切り分ける。
cue: You are giving a cooking instruction.
reply: Chop up the onions while the oil heats.
replyJapanese: 油が温まるあいだに、玉ねぎを細かく切ってください。
transferCue: Describe preparing firewood.
transferReply: He chopped up the old fence for kindling.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は古い塀を、焚きつけ用に細かく割りました。
nuance: Separable: chop them up. The up signals thoroughness — into many pieces.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：chop them up。up は「細かく全部」という徹底のニュアンスを加える。
contrast: Chop up cuts into pieces; cut up is the more general everyday verb.
contrastJapanese: chop up は細かく刻む。cut up はより一般的な日常語。

meaning: Throw something away, or make someone leave.
japanese: 捨てる。また、追い出す。
cue: You are clearing a cupboard with a housemate.
reply: Shall we chuck out anything older than two years?
replyJapanese: 2年以上前のものは、捨ててしまいましょうか。
transferCue: Describe a venue closing at night.
transferReply: They chuck everyone out at eleven.
transferReplyJapanese: 11時には、全員が外に出されます。
nuance: Separable: chuck it out. Informal and British; throw out is the neutral version.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：chuck it out。くだけたイギリス英語で、中立的な言い方は throw out。
contrast: Chuck out is informal discarding; clear out empties a whole space.
contrastJapanese: chuck out はくだけた「捨てる」。clear out は場所全体を空にする。

meaning: Become covered with cloud, or become unhappy.
japanese: 雲に覆われる。また、表情が曇る。
cue: Describe a change in the weather during a walk.
reply: It clouded over just as we reached the top.
replyJapanese: 頂上に着いたちょうどそのとき、空が曇りました。
transferCue: Describe someone's reaction to bad news.
transferReply: His face clouded over when he read the message.
transferReplyJapanese: メッセージを読んだとき、彼の顔が曇りました。
nuance: Intransitive. The sky or someone's face is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。主語は空か、人の表情。
contrast: Cloud over is the sky or a face darkening; blow over is a problem passing.
contrastJapanese: cloud over は空や表情が曇ること。blow over は問題が過ぎ去ること。

meaning: Fill a space untidily with things.
japanese: 物でいっぱいにして、雑然とさせる。
cue: A hallway has become impassable. Suggest a change.
reply: These boxes are cluttering up the hall.
replyJapanese: この箱が、玄関を雑然とさせています。
transferCue: Describe an overloaded screen.
transferReply: Too many icons clutter up the desktop.
transferReplyJapanese: アイコンが多すぎて、画面が雑然としています。
nuance: Separable: clutter it up. The things, not the person, are usually the subject.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：clutter it up。主語はふつう人ではなく、物のほう。
contrast: Clutter up fills untidily; tidy up is the opposite action.
contrastJapanese: clutter up は雑然とさせる。tidy up はその反対の行為。

meaning: Gently persuade someone to give you something.
japanese: やさしく説得して、引き出す。
cue: A quiet child eventually told you what happened. Describe it.
reply: It took an hour to coax the story out of him.
replyJapanese: 話を聞き出すまでに、1時間かかりました。
transferCue: Describe getting information from a reluctant colleague.
transferReply: She coaxed the real reason out of them over coffee.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はコーヒーを飲みながら、本当の理由を引き出しました。
nuance: The thing goes between coax and out of, and the person follows. It implies gentleness, not pressure.
nuanceJapanese: 引き出すものは coax と out of のあいだに置き、相手をそのあとに続ける。圧力ではなく、やさしさを含む。
contrast: Coax out of persuades gently; drag out of implies real resistance.
contrastJapanese: coax out of はやさしく引き出す。drag out of は強い抵抗を押しての場合に使う。

meaning: Give formal permission for something.
japanese: 正式に同意する。承諾する。
cue: A client approved a change in writing. Report it.
reply: They consented to the revised schedule yesterday.
replyJapanese: 先方は昨日、修正後の日程に同意しました。
transferCue: Describe a permission form.
transferReply: Parents must consent to the trip in writing.
transferReplyJapanese: 保護者は、書面で旅行に同意する必要があります。
nuance: Inseparable and formal, followed by a noun or -ing. Agree to is the everyday version.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない改まった表現で、名詞か -ing を続ける。日常では agree to を使う。
contrast: Consent to is formal permission; agree to is ordinary acceptance.
contrastJapanese: consent to は正式な許可。agree to はふつうの了承。

meaning: Match or be equivalent to something.
japanese: 〜に対応している。一致する。
cue: Two sets of numbers should match. Report a check.
reply: The totals correspond to the figures in the appendix.
replyJapanese: 合計は、付録の数字と一致しています。
transferCue: Explain a colour-coded chart.
transferReply: Each colour corresponds to one department.
transferReplyJapanese: それぞれの色が、ひとつの部署に対応しています。
nuance: Inseparable. Correspond with can mean the same, but also means exchanging letters.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。correspond with も同じ意味で使えるが、「文通する」の意味にもなる。
contrast: Correspond to matches something; amount to means adding up to a total or result.
contrastJapanese: correspond to は対応・一致する。amount to は合計や結果になる。

meaning: Count backwards to a moment, or wait eagerly for it.
japanese: その時まで数えて待つ。心待ちにする。
cue: A friend asks how you feel about an upcoming holiday.
reply: I'm counting down to Friday already.
replyJapanese: もう金曜が待ち遠しいです。
transferCue: Describe the final seconds of a new year.
transferReply: Everyone counted down from ten.
transferReplyJapanese: みんなで10から数えました。
nuance: Intransitive. To introduces the awaited moment. The noun is a countdown, written as one word.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。待っている時点は to で示す。名詞は countdown と1語で書く。
contrast: Count down waits for a moment; count on relies on someone.
contrastJapanese: count down はその時を待つ。count on は人を頼りにする。

meaning: Produce a lot of something quickly.
japanese: 量産する。次々に作り出す。
cue: A writer publishes very frequently. Describe it.
reply: He cranks out a column every week.
replyJapanese: 彼は毎週、コラムを量産しています。
transferCue: Describe a busy print shop.
transferReply: They cranked out two thousand leaflets in a day.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは1日で、チラシを2000枚刷り上げました。
nuance: Separable: crank them out. Informal and mostly American, often implying routine rather than care.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：crank them out。くだけた主にアメリカ英語で、丁寧さより機械的な量産を含意することが多い。
contrast: Crank out is fast repeated production; churn out adds a stronger hint of low quality.
contrastJapanese: crank out は速く繰り返し作ること。churn out は質の低さをより強く含む。

meaning: Take the best part of something for yourself.
japanese: いちばんよい部分だけを、先に取る。
cue: A scheme takes the strongest applicants from local schools. Describe it critically.
reply: The programme creams off the best students.
replyJapanese: その制度は、優秀な生徒だけを先に取っていきます。
transferCue: Describe how a fee affects earnings.
transferReply: The platform creams off a third of every payment.
transferReplyJapanese: あのプラットフォームは、支払いのたびに3分の1を抜いていきます。
nuance: Separable: cream them off. British and usually disapproving.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：cream them off。イギリス英語で、ふつうは否定的に使う。
contrast: Cream off takes the best share; siphon off diverts a portion quietly.
contrastJapanese: cream off は良いところを取る。siphon off はひそかに一部を抜き取る。

meaning: Move successfully from one field or audience to another.
japanese: 別の分野や客層へ、うまく移る。
cue: A specialist product found a general audience. Describe it.
reply: The brand crossed over into mainstream shops.
replyJapanese: そのブランドは、一般の店にも広がりました。
transferCue: Describe a musician changing genre.
transferReply: She crossed over from jazz to film scores.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はジャズから映画音楽へと移りました。
nuance: Intransitive. Into or from introduces the fields. The noun is a crossover.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。分野は into や from で示す。名詞は crossover。
contrast: Cross over moves between fields; branch out expands without leaving the first.
contrastJapanese: cross over は分野を移る。branch out は元を残したまま広げる。

meaning: Write or produce something very quickly.
japanese: さっと手早く書き上げる。
cue: A short note is needed before you leave.
reply: Let me dash off a quick reply before we go.
replyJapanese: 出る前に、返事をさっと書いてしまいます。
transferCue: Describe a thank-you card written in a hurry.
transferReply: I dashed off a card at the station.
transferReplyJapanese: 駅でカードをさっと書きました。
nuance: Separable: dash it off. Dash off alone can also mean leaving somewhere in a hurry.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：dash it off。目的語なしの dash off は「急いで立ち去る」の意味にもなる。
contrast: Dash off writes quickly; jot down records a few words as a note.
contrastJapanese: dash off は手早く書き上げる。jot down は短くメモを取る。

meaning: Buy and sell a particular kind of thing.
japanese: ある種類の商品を扱う。
cue: Explain what a shop specialises in.
reply: They deal in second-hand instruments.
replyJapanese: あの店は、中古の楽器を扱っています。
transferCue: Describe a firm's focus.
transferReply: We deal in commercial property only.
transferReplyJapanese: 当社は、商業用不動産のみを扱っています。
nuance: Inseparable. Deal in facts or rumours extends it to what someone trades in figuratively.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。deal in facts、deal in rumours のように、比喩的に「扱う対象」を表すこともできる。
contrast: Deal in names what you trade; deal with handles a problem or a person.
contrastJapanese: deal in は扱う商品を示す。deal with は問題や相手に対応する。

meaning: Give your time or effort entirely to something.
japanese: 時間や労力を、そのために捧げる。
cue: Explain how you protect time for a long project.
reply: I dedicate Saturday mornings to the thesis.
replyJapanese: 土曜の午前は、論文のために充てています。
transferCue: Describe a building's dedication.
transferReply: The hall is dedicated to the founder.
transferReplyJapanese: あのホールは、創設者に捧げられています。
nuance: The thing given goes between dedicate and to. Also used for books and buildings honouring a person.
nuanceJapanese: 捧げるものは dedicate と to のあいだに置く。本や建物を人に献じる意味でも使う。
contrast: Dedicate to commits time or honour; devote to is a close everyday alternative.
contrastJapanese: dedicate to は時間を充てる、または献じる。devote to はほぼ同じ意味の日常語。

meaning: Find something that was stored away.
japanese: しまい込んでいたものを、探し出す。
cue: A friend asks whether you still have an old photograph.
reply: I'll dig out the album this weekend.
replyJapanese: 今週末に、アルバムを引っぱり出します。
transferCue: Describe preparing for cold weather.
transferReply: I dug out my winter coat in October.
transferReplyJapanese: 10月に、冬のコートを引っぱり出しました。
nuance: Separable: dig it out. Dig is irregular: dug. It implies the thing was stored, not lost.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：dig it out。dig は不規則変化で dug。なくしたのではなく、しまってあったものを指す。
contrast: Dig out retrieves something stored; dig up uncovers information.
contrastJapanese: dig out はしまってあった物を出す。dig up は情報を掘り起こす。

meaning: Eat a meal in a restaurant.
japanese: 外食する。
cue: A visitor asks about local habits.
reply: People here dine out more on Fridays than at weekends.
replyJapanese: このあたりでは、週末より金曜に外食する人が多いです。
transferCue: Describe a change in your routine.
transferReply: We dine out far less than we used to.
transferReplyJapanese: 以前より、外食はずっと減りました。
nuance: Intransitive and slightly formal; eat out is the everyday version. Dine out on a story means retelling it often.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でやや改まった表現。日常では eat out と言う。dine out on a story なら、その話を繰り返し披露する意味。
contrast: Dine out is formal for eating at a restaurant; eat out is the ordinary phrase.
contrastJapanese: dine out は改まった言い方。eat out がふつうの表現。

meaning: Serve food onto plates.
japanese: 料理を皿に盛って出す。
cue: Dinner is ready and guests are waiting.
reply: I'll dish up while you pour the water.
replyJapanese: 水を注いでもらえたら、私が盛りつけます。
transferCue: Describe timing a meal.
transferReply: Dish up as soon as the rice is done.
transferReplyJapanese: ご飯が炊けたら、すぐに盛りつけてください。
nuance: Separable: dish it up. Informal. It can also mean presenting the same content repeatedly.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：dish it up。くだけた表現で、同じ内容を繰り返し出す意味にもなる。
contrast: Dish up puts food on plates; serve up can also describe offering something for criticism.
contrastJapanese: dish up は皿に盛る。serve up は批判の対象として差し出す意味にも使う。

meaning: Start doing something with great energy.
japanese: 勢いよく、すぐに取りかかる。
cue: A colleague began a task immediately. Describe it.
reply: She dived into the data before anyone else arrived.
replyJapanese: 誰よりも早く、彼女はデータに取りかかりました。
transferCue: Advise caution before starting quickly.
transferReply: Let's not dive into the code before we agree the shape.
transferReplyJapanese: 全体像を決める前に、いきなりコードに取りかからないようにしましょう。
nuance: Inseparable. Both dived and dove are used as the past form.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。過去形は dived と dove のどちらも使われる。
contrast: Dive into starts energetically; delve into examines something in depth.
contrastJapanese: dive into は勢いよく始める。delve into は深く掘り下げて調べる。

meaning: Make someone extremely tired.
japanese: へとへとに疲れさせる。
cue: A long day of moving furniture has ended.
reply: That staircase has done me in.
replyJapanese: あの階段で、へとへとになりました。
transferCue: Describe a colleague after a long shift.
transferReply: Three nights in a row would do anyone in.
transferReplyJapanese: 3晩続けば、誰でもへとへとになります。
nuance: Separable: do me in. Informal and often in the passive: I'm done in.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：do me in。くだけた表現で、I'm done in のように受け身でよく使う。
contrast: Do in is exhaustion; wear out can also describe objects becoming unusable.
contrastJapanese: do in は疲れ果てること。wear out は物が使えなくなる意味にも使う。

meaning: Gradually disappear or become less.
japanese: 少しずつ消えてなくなる。
cue: Enthusiasm faded over a long project. Describe it.
reply: The energy drained away after the third delay.
replyJapanese: 3度目の遅れのあと、勢いは失われていきました。
transferCue: Describe savings during a difficult year.
transferReply: Our reserves drained away over eight months.
transferReplyJapanese: 8か月のあいだに、蓄えは少しずつ減っていきました。
nuance: Intransitive. The thing lost is the subject, and it implies a slow, unnoticed decline.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。主語は失われるもので、気づかぬうちに少しずつ減る含みがある。
contrast: Drain away is gradual loss; dry up is a supply stopping altogether.
contrastJapanese: drain away は徐々に減ること。dry up は供給が完全に止まること。

meaning: Become dark earlier as winter approaches.
japanese: 日が短くなる。
cue: Comment on the season in late October.
reply: The evenings are drawing in already.
replyJapanese: もう日が短くなってきましたね。
transferCue: Explain a change to an outdoor schedule.
transferReply: As the nights draw in we'll move training indoors.
transferReplyJapanese: 日が短くなってきたら、練習は屋内に移します。
nuance: Intransitive, British, and almost always with evenings or nights as the subject.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でイギリス英語。主語はほぼつねに evenings か nights。
contrast: Draw in is days getting shorter; close in is something threatening approaching.
contrastJapanese: draw in は日が短くなること。close in は脅威が迫ること。

meaning: Examine the details beneath a summary.
japanese: 概要の下にある詳細まで、掘り下げて見る。
cue: A headline figure hides useful detail. Propose a next step.
reply: Let's drill down into the regional numbers.
replyJapanese: 地域別の数字まで掘り下げてみましょう。
transferCue: Describe reviewing a household budget.
transferReply: We drilled down and found three forgotten subscriptions.
transferReplyJapanese: 細かく見ていったら、忘れていた定期購読が3つ見つかりました。
nuance: Intransitive, usually with into. Common in data and business contexts.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、ふつう into を伴う。データや業務の文脈でよく使う。
contrast: Drill down goes from summary to detail; delve into explores a subject broadly.
contrastJapanese: drill down は概要から詳細へ降りる。delve into は主題を広く深く探る。

meaning: Finish your drink.
japanese: 飲み物を飲み干す。
cue: A group needs to leave a café soon.
reply: Drink up — the last train is at eleven.
replyJapanese: 飲んでしまいましょう。終電は11時です。
transferCue: Encourage a child at breakfast.
transferReply: Drink up your milk before the bus comes.
transferReplyJapanese: バスが来る前に、牛乳を飲んでしまいなさい。
nuance: Separable: drink it up. The up means finish it completely, not just drink.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：drink it up。up は単に飲むのではなく「飲み干す」ことを表す。
contrast: Drink up finishes a drink; drink in means absorbing a scene or words eagerly.
contrastJapanese: drink up は飲み干す。drink in は景色や言葉に見入る・聞き入ること。

meaning: Survive a difficult period without serious harm.
japanese: 厳しい時期を、持ちこたえて乗り切る。
cue: A business faces a slow quarter. Describe the plan.
reply: We'll ride out the slow months with the reserve.
replyJapanese: 閑散期は、蓄えで乗り切ります。
transferCue: Describe a boat in bad weather.
transferReply: The crew rode out the storm in the harbour.
transferReplyJapanese: 乗組員は港で嵐をやり過ごしました。
nuance: Separable: ride it out. Ride is irregular: rode, ridden. It implies enduring, not solving.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：ride it out。ride は不規則変化で rode、ridden。解決ではなく耐えることを表す。
contrast: Ride out endures a bad period; see out means staying until the end of a term.
contrastJapanese: ride out は困難を耐え抜く。see out は期間の終わりまで務め上げる。

meaning: Warn people that something is seriously wrong.
japanese: 重大な問題があると、警鐘を鳴らす。
cue: A researcher warned about a risk years ago. Describe it.
reply: She sounded the alarm about the leak in 2022.
replyJapanese: 彼女は2022年に、その漏えいについて警鐘を鳴らしました。
transferCue: Describe a colleague raising a concern early.
transferReply: Someone sounded the alarm before the figures were published.
transferReplyJapanese: 数字が公表される前に、誰かが警鐘を鳴らしていました。
nuance: About or over introduces the danger. Slightly more public and urgent than raise the alarm.
nuanceJapanese: 危険の内容は about か over で示す。raise the alarm より公的で、切迫した響きがある。
contrast: Sound the alarm warns publicly; raise the alarm alerts the people who need to act.
contrastJapanese: sound the alarm は広く警告する。raise the alarm は対応すべき人に知らせる。

meaning: Gradually become less acceptable or less convincing.
japanese: だんだん通用しなくなる。我慢の限界に近づく。
cue: The same excuse has been used three times. Comment.
reply: That explanation is wearing thin.
replyJapanese: その説明は、そろそろ通用しなくなってきました。
transferCue: Describe a running joke that has lasted too long.
transferReply: The joke wore thin after the second week.
transferReplyJapanese: その冗談は、2週目を過ぎて飽きられました。
nuance: Intransitive. Wear is irregular: wore, worn. Patience wears thin is a very common collocation.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。wear は不規則変化で wore、worn。patience wears thin の形が非常によく使われる。
contrast: Wear thin is losing acceptability; wear off is an effect fading away.
contrastJapanese: wear thin は通用しなくなること。wear off は効果が薄れること。

meaning: Continue with something difficult or dull.
japanese: 大変でも、構わず進め続ける。
cue: A long task is tedious but must be finished.
reply: Let's plough on and finish the last twenty pages.
replyJapanese: 構わず進めて、残り20ページを片づけましょう。
transferCue: Describe reading a difficult book.
transferReply: I ploughed on to the end and was glad I did.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後まで読み通して、読んでよかったと思いました。
nuance: Intransitive and British; American English spells it plow. With introduces the task.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でイギリス英語。アメリカ英語では plow とつづる。対象は with で示す。
contrast: Plough on continues through tedium; press on continues despite obstacles.
contrastJapanese: plough on は退屈でも進め続ける。press on は障害があっても進み続ける。

meaning: Find something extremely valuable or successful.
japanese: 大当たりを引き当てる。
cue: One hire transformed a team. Describe it.
reply: We struck gold when we hired her.
replyJapanese: 彼女を採用したのは、大当たりでした。
transferCue: Describe finding the right supplier.
transferReply: After four trials we struck gold.
transferReplyJapanese: 4回試して、ようやく当たりを引きました。
nuance: Strike is irregular: struck. Gold takes no article, and the phrase is figurative.
nuanceJapanese: strike は不規則変化で struck。gold に冠詞は付かず、比喩的に使う。
contrast: Strike gold finds something valuable; hit the jackpot stresses luck and scale.
contrastJapanese: strike gold は価値あるものを見つける。hit the jackpot は運と規模を強調する。

meaning: Become established and start to grow.
japanese: 根づいて、定着し始める。
cue: A new habit has become normal in a team. Describe it.
reply: The new routine has taken root across the office.
replyJapanese: 新しい手順が、事務所全体に根づきました。
transferCue: Describe an idea spreading in a community.
transferReply: The idea took root long before anyone funded it.
transferReplyJapanese: その考えは、誰かが出資するずっと前から根づいていました。
nuance: Root takes no article and stays singular. The idea or practice is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: root に冠詞は付かず、単数のまま。主語は考えや習慣のほう。
contrast: Take root becomes established; catch on becomes widely popular.
contrastJapanese: take root は定着する。catch on は広く流行する。

meaning: Behave too freely with something or someone.
japanese: 勝手が過ぎる。度を越して自由に扱う。
cue: An adaptation changed the original story heavily. Comment.
reply: The film takes liberties with the book.
replyJapanese: あの映画は、原作をかなり自由に改変しています。
transferCue: Describe someone overusing a shared resource.
transferReply: He's taking liberties with the office car.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は社用車を、少し勝手に使いすぎています。
nuance: Liberties is always plural. With introduces what is treated too freely. Usually critical.
nuanceJapanese: liberties はつねに複数形。対象は with で示す。ふつうは批判的な表現。
contrast: Take liberties is overstepping; take advantage of exploits a person or a situation.
contrastJapanese: take liberties は度を越すこと。take advantage of は人や状況につけ込むこと。

meaning: Have a surprisingly good effect.
japanese: 驚くほどよく効く。
cue: A simple remedy helped a friend's cold.
reply: Honey and lemon worked wonders.
replyJapanese: はちみつとレモンが、驚くほど効きました。
transferCue: Describe a small change at work.
transferReply: Moving the meeting to Tuesday worked wonders.
transferReplyJapanese: 会議を火曜に移したら、驚くほどうまくいきました。
nuance: Wonders is always plural. For introduces who or what benefits.
nuanceJapanese: wonders はつねに複数形。効果の及ぶ対象は for で示す。
contrast: Work wonders is a surprisingly good effect; do the trick is simply sufficient.
contrastJapanese: work wonders は驚くほど効く。do the trick は必要十分という意味。

meaning: Forget past mistakes and start again.
japanese: 過去の失敗を帳消しにして、やり直す。
cue: Two colleagues want a fresh start after a dispute.
reply: Let's wipe the slate clean and start again on Monday.
replyJapanese: 過去のことは帳消しにして、月曜からやり直しましょう。
transferCue: Describe a debt settlement.
transferReply: The final payment wiped the slate clean.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の支払いで、すべて帳消しになりました。
nuance: Slate takes the and stays singular. It proposes forgetting, not forgiving in detail.
nuanceJapanese: slate には the を付け、単数のまま。細かく許すというより、忘れて仕切り直すことを提案する。
contrast: Wipe the slate clean erases the past; draw a line under closes a chapter without erasing it.
contrastJapanese: wipe the slate clean は過去を帳消しにする。draw a line under は消さずに区切りをつける。

meaning: Consider carefully before deciding.
japanese: よく考え直してから決める。
cue: A friend is about to sign something quickly. Advise caution.
reply: I'd think twice before signing a three-year term.
replyJapanese: 3年契約に署名する前に、よく考え直したほうがいいでしょう。
transferCue: Describe how a bad experience changed you.
transferReply: I think twice about booking non-refundable fares now.
transferReplyJapanese: 今は、払い戻し不可の運賃を取る前によく考えます。
nuance: Twice never changes. Before plus -ing, or about plus -ing, introduces the action.
nuanceJapanese: twice の形は変わらない。行動は before＋-ing か about＋-ing で示す。
contrast: Think twice hesitates before acting; think over weighs a proposal already made.
contrastJapanese: think twice は行動前にためらうこと。think over はすでに出た提案を検討すること。

meaning: Use your authority in an unpleasant way.
japanese: 権威をかさに着て、いばる。
cue: A senior colleague pressured a junior unfairly. Describe it.
reply: He was throwing his weight around in front of the new starters.
replyJapanese: 彼は新人の前で、権威をかさに着ていばっていました。
transferCue: Describe how you want to lead a team.
transferReply: I don't want to throw my weight around on day one.
transferReplyJapanese: 初日から、権威をかさに着るようなことはしたくありません。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Always disapproving, and usually about someone senior.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。つねに否定的で、立場が上の人について使うのがふつう。
contrast: Throw your weight around abuses authority; stand your ground defends a position.
contrastJapanese: throw your weight around は権威を振りかざす。stand your ground は自分の立場を守る。

meaning: Produce a good result when it was not expected.
japanese: 思いがけず、よい結果を出す。
cue: Someone unexpectedly solved a problem. Praise them.
reply: Maya turned up trumps with a spare projector.
replyJapanese: マヤさんが予備のプロジェクターを出してくれて、助かりました。
transferCue: Describe a backup plan that worked.
transferReply: The second supplier turned up trumps in the end.
transferReplyJapanese: 結局、2番目の業者が期待以上にやってくれました。
nuance: British and informal. Trumps is always plural, and come up trumps is equally common.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。trumps はつねに複数形で、come up trumps も同じくらいよく使う。
contrast: Turn up trumps is an unexpected good result; come through is delivering when relied on.
contrastJapanese: turn up trumps は予想外の好結果。come through は頼られて期待に応えること。

meaning: Control something so it does not grow or become known.
japanese: 表に出ないよう、抑えておく。
cue: Costs must not rise further this quarter. State the goal.
reply: We need to keep a lid on costs until March.
replyJapanese: 3月まで、費用を抑えておく必要があります。
transferCue: Describe managing a rumour.
transferReply: They kept a lid on the news for a fortnight.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは2週間、その知らせを外に出しませんでした。
nuance: On introduces what is controlled. Used for costs, emotions and information alike.
nuanceJapanese: 抑える対象は on で示す。費用にも感情にも情報にも使う。
contrast: Keep a lid on contains something; bottle up holds feelings in until they build.
contrastJapanese: keep a lid on は全般を抑え込む。bottle up は感情をため込むこと。

meaning: Stay informed about the latest developments.
japanese: 最新の動きを、把握し続ける。
cue: A colleague asks how you follow changes in your field.
reply: I keep abreast of the guidance through one newsletter.
replyJapanese: ひとつの会報で、指針の変更を把握しています。
transferCue: Describe a requirement in a job description.
transferReply: You'll need to keep abreast of the regulations.
transferReplyJapanese: 規制の動きを把握し続ける必要があります。
nuance: Inseparable and formal. Of introduces the subject; stay and remain work the same way.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない改まった表現。対象は of で示し、stay や remain でも同じように使える。
contrast: Keep abreast of follows developments; keep up with can also mean matching a pace.
contrastJapanese: keep abreast of は動向を追う。keep up with には速さについていく意味もある。

meaning: Try hard to make something succeed.
japanese: なんとか成功させようと努める。
cue: A friend has taken over a struggling shop. Wish them well.
reply: I hope they make a go of it.
replyJapanese: うまくいくといいですね。
transferCue: Describe a couple moving to a new town.
transferReply: They're determined to make a go of it there.
transferReplyJapanese: 二人はあそこで、なんとかやっていくつもりです。
nuance: Usually with it. Informal, and it implies effort with an uncertain outcome.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう it を伴う。くだけた表現で、結果が不確かななかでの努力を含意する。
contrast: Make a go of is trying to succeed; pull off means actually achieving something difficult.
contrastJapanese: make a go of は成功させようと努めること。pull off は実際に成し遂げること。

meaning: Stop being as good at something as you were.
japanese: 以前ほどうまくできなくなる。
cue: You made an uncharacteristic mistake. Joke about it.
reply: Two errors in a week — I'm losing my touch.
replyJapanese: 1週間で2回も間違えました。腕が鈍ったようです。
transferCue: Praise someone whose skill has not faded.
transferReply: Thirty years on and she hasn't lost her touch.
transferReplyJapanese: 30年経っても、彼女の腕は少しも鈍っていません。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Often used lightly about yourself, or in the negative as praise.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。自分について軽く使うか、否定形でほめる形が多い。
contrast: Lose your touch is losing skill; lose your nerve is losing courage.
contrastJapanese: lose your touch は腕が鈍ること。lose your nerve は勇気を失うこと。

meaning: Develop fully and be taken seriously.
japanese: 一人前になる。認められる段階に達する。
cue: A once-niche technology is now standard. Describe the shift.
reply: Electric vans have come of age in the last five years.
replyJapanese: 電動バンは、この5年で一人前の選択肢になりました。
transferCue: Describe a young musician's development.
transferReply: She came of age as a performer on that tour.
transferReplyJapanese: あのツアーで、彼女は演奏家として一人前になりました。
nuance: Age takes no article. It also has a legal sense of reaching adulthood.
nuanceJapanese: age に冠詞は付かない。法的に成人に達するという意味もある。
contrast: Come of age is reaching full development; come into your own is performing well in the right conditions.
contrastJapanese: come of age は十分に成熟すること。come into your own は条件が整って本領を発揮すること。

meaning: Change financial records dishonestly.
japanese: 帳簿をごまかす。
cue: An audit uncovered falsified records. Describe the finding.
reply: The audit found that someone had cooked the books.
replyJapanese: 監査で、帳簿がごまかされていたことが分かりました。
transferCue: Explain why records are checked independently.
transferReply: Separate review makes it much harder to cook the books.
transferReplyJapanese: 第三者の確認があると、帳簿のごまかしはずっと難しくなります。
nuance: Books is always plural and takes the. A serious accusation, so keep it for actual fraud.
nuanceJapanese: books はつねに複数形で the を伴う。重い告発なので、実際の不正に限って使う。
contrast: Cook the books falsifies accounts; massage the figures presents real data favourably.
contrastJapanese: cook the books は帳簿の改ざん。massage the figures は本当の数字を有利に見せること。

meaning: Cry a great deal.
japanese: さんざん泣く。泣きはらす。
cue: Describe a child's reaction to a lost toy.
reply: She cried her eyes out for an hour.
replyJapanese: 彼女は1時間、泣きはらしていました。
transferCue: Describe a film that moved you.
transferReply: I cried my eyes out at the ending.
transferReplyJapanese: あの結末では、さんざん泣きました。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and eyes is plural. Informal and hyperbolic.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、eyes は複数形。くだけた大げさな言い方。
contrast: Cry your eyes out is prolonged crying; well up is tears just beginning.
contrastJapanese: cry your eyes out は長く泣くこと。well up は涙が浮かび始めること。

meaning: Reach an agreement, often after negotiation.
japanese: 交渉の末に、取引をまとめる。
cue: Two sides reached terms after a long negotiation. Report it.
reply: They cut a deal on Friday evening.
replyJapanese: 金曜の夕方、双方は取引をまとめました。
transferCue: Describe settling a dispute out of court.
transferReply: Both sides cut a deal rather than go to court.
transferReplyJapanese: 両者は裁判を避けて、話をまとめました。
nuance: Informal, mostly American. With introduces the other party, and on introduces the subject.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた主にアメリカ英語。相手は with、対象は on で示す。
contrast: Cut a deal reaches terms; seal the deal completes an agreement already close.
contrastJapanese: cut a deal は条件をまとめる。seal the deal はまとまりかけた話を成立させる。

meaning: Join in something after others have started it.
japanese: あとから加わって、自分も一枚かむ。
cue: Several competitors copied a successful idea. Describe it.
reply: Three other firms wanted to get in on the act.
replyJapanese: ほかに3社が、その流れに乗ろうとしました。
transferCue: Describe family members joining a hobby.
transferReply: Once I started baking, everyone got in on the act.
transferReplyJapanese: 私がパンを焼き始めたら、みんなが加わってきました。
nuance: Informal. Often mildly critical of latecomers, though it can be affectionate.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現。後から来た人への軽い批判になることが多いが、親しみを込めても使える。
contrast: Get in on the act joins something already happening; jump on the bandwagon stresses following a trend.
contrastJapanese: get in on the act は進行中のことに加わる。jump on the bandwagon は流行に乗ることを強調する。

meaning: Try as hard as you can.
japanese: できるかぎり全力でやってみる。
cue: A friend is nervous before an audition. Encourage them.
reply: Give it your best shot and see what happens.
replyJapanese: 全力でやってみて、結果を見ましょう。
transferCue: Describe your attitude to a difficult exam.
transferReply: I gave it my best shot and that's all I could do.
transferReplyJapanese: 全力を尽くしました。できることはそれだけでした。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Informal and encouraging, and it accepts that the result is uncertain.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。くだけた励ましの表現で、結果が不確かなことを受け入れている。
contrast: Give it your best shot is a full attempt; have a go is a lighter, casual try.
contrastJapanese: give it your best shot は全力での挑戦。have a go はもっと気軽な試み。

meaning: The people in authority, whoever they are.
japanese: 上の人たち。お偉方。
cue: A decision came from somewhere above your team.
reply: The powers that be have moved the deadline again.
replyJapanese: 上のほうで、また締め切りが動かされました。
transferCue: Explain why a rule cannot be changed locally.
transferReply: That's for the powers that be to decide, not us.
transferReplyJapanese: それは私たちではなく、上の人たちが決めることです。
nuance: Fixed and always plural with the. Mildly resigned or ironic about distant authority.
nuanceJapanese: the を伴う固定表現で、つねに複数扱い。遠い権威に対する、あきらめや皮肉を含む。
contrast: The powers that be is vague authority; the management names a specific group.
contrastJapanese: the powers that be は漠然とした上層部。the management は特定の集団を指す。

meaning: The most important quality or aim in a situation.
japanese: その場面で、いちばん肝心なこと。
cue: Explain what matters most in a fast-moving project.
reply: Speed is the name of the game this quarter.
replyJapanese: この四半期は、速さが何より肝心です。
transferCue: Describe what a sport demands.
transferReply: In long-distance running, patience is the name of the game.
transferReplyJapanese: 長距離走では、忍耐がいちばん肝心です。
frame: X is the name of the game
nuance: The quality comes first, then the phrase. Informal and always singular.
nuanceJapanese: 先に肝心な要素を置き、そのあとにこの表現を続ける。くだけた言い方で、つねに単数。
contrast: The name of the game is what matters most; the bottom line is the final financial result.
contrastJapanese: the name of the game は最重要点。the bottom line は最終的な収支や結論。

meaning: Without any problems at all.
japanese: 何の問題もなく。滞りなく。
cue: An event you were worried about went perfectly. Report it.
reply: The whole day went without a hitch.
replyJapanese: その日は一日、何の問題もなく進みました。
transferCue: Describe a move you expected to be difficult.
transferReply: The move went without a hitch, to our surprise.
transferReplyJapanese: 意外にも、引っ越しは滞りなく終わりました。
nuance: Almost always with go. A hitch keeps its article, and the phrase is fixed.
nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに go と一緒に使う。a hitch の冠詞は省かず、形は固定。
contrast: Without a hitch means nothing went wrong; up and running means something is now working.
contrastJapanese: without a hitch は問題が起きなかったこと。up and running は動き始めている状態。

meaning: Very angry and protesting about something.
japanese: 強く怒って、抗議している。
cue: Residents objected loudly to a parking change. Describe it.
reply: The whole street is up in arms about the new charges.
replyJapanese: 通り全体が、新しい料金に強く抗議しています。
transferCue: Describe staff reaction to a policy.
transferReply: Everyone was up in arms when the notice went out.
transferReplyJapanese: 通知が出たとき、全員が強く反発しました。
frame: Be up in arms about something
nuance: Arms is always plural. About or over introduces the cause, and it describes a group rather than one person.
nuanceJapanese: arms はつねに複数形。原因は about か over で示し、個人より集団について使う。
contrast: Up in arms is collective protest; see red is one person's sudden anger.
contrastJapanese: up in arms は集団の抗議。see red は個人の突発的な怒り。

meaning: Already achieved or experienced.
japanese: すでに身につけている。経験済みである。
cue: A colleague asks whether you are ready for a bigger role.
reply: With two years under my belt I feel ready.
replyJapanese: 2年の経験を積んで、準備はできたと思います。
transferCue: Describe a runner before a race.
transferReply: She has three marathons under her belt.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はマラソンを3回完走しています。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually with have, and it counts completed experience.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。ふつう have と一緒に使い、積んだ経験を数える。
contrast: Under your belt counts what you have done; up your sleeve is something you are keeping in reserve.
contrastJapanese: under your belt は積んだ経験。up your sleeve は隠し持っている切り札。

meaning: Delay judging until you know more.
japanese: 様子を見てから判断する。
cue: A colleague asks for a decision you cannot make yet.
reply: Let's wait and see what the figures look like on Monday.
replyJapanese: 月曜の数字を見てから決めましょう。
transferCue: Answer a child asking about a possible trip.
transferReply: We'll have to wait and see what the weather does.
transferReplyJapanese: 天気がどうなるか、様子を見ましょう。
nuance: The two verbs stay together in that order. It postpones judgement without refusing.
nuanceJapanese: 2つの動詞はこの順でひとまとまりに使う。拒否ではなく、判断を先送りする表現。
contrast: Wait and see delays judgement; hold off delays an action.
contrastJapanese: wait and see は判断を保留する。hold off は行動を先延ばしする。
